content.section: Why AI Literacy Matters in Education
content.text: An AI curriculum for schools, grounded in AI literacy,is no longer optional -- it is fundamental. Let me define AI literacy simply: AI literacy is the ability to understand, use, evaluate, and critically reflect upon AI applications. Schools must implement an AI curriculum by providing relevant education to students, because as functions of AI become more available with generative models or through the use of chatbots and immersive personalized learning plans, students need to know not only how to use it but the ethical implications of AI Effective AI literacy helps students:
points: Develop critical thinking skills to recognize biases and limitations of AI outputs.
Co-create with AI tools to improve problem-solving and creativity.
Learn how to assess AI systems and make ethical decisions with respect to AI.

China: Since late 2024, schools have been required to offer at least 8 hours of AI instruction each year, staged by age: from simple exposure in the primary years to project-based AI learning in the high school year

outh Korea & Singapore:Using adaptive AI textbooks, and developing adaptive AI teacher training, South Korea is embedding AI in all K–12 levels. Singapore is rolling-out AI for Fun modules, embedding ethics education across subjects, and training all teachers by 2026.
